extracted.intended_audience: PR and marketing professionals creating multichannel news releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and measuring multichannel news releases (MNRs): branded, multimedia-rich press-release landing pages optimized for distribution, accessibility, and performance measurement. Includes recommendations on structure, assets, accessibility, measurement and when to use MNRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: MNR composition (branded landing pages & distribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Multichannel News Release (MNR) consists of branded landing pages and content distribution solutions, which serve as the hub for multichannel marketing. MNRs include multimedia assets, branding and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the release page as a content hub combining owned assets and distribution; ensure branding is clear and that the page functions as the central place for the story and assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedded assets throughout the text body
rubrics_metrics.description: An MNR should include embedded video, audio and interactive features within the text body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed videos and images throughout the text to break up content and make it easier to scan; enable viewing/listening/scrolling without leaving the release page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive features (clickable infographics, visualizations, social sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clickable infographics, data visualizations and social sharing buttons allow the user to engage with the data directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include interactive elements that let readers explore or share data; prioritize interactivity that clarifies complex information or encourages distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear hierarchy (headlines, subheads, bullet points)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines, subheads and bullet points guide the reader through the narrative while visuals act as anchors for key sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use typographic hierarchy and visuals as anchors so readers can scan and find key information quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile-first formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The design adapts automatically to smaller screens and stacks content logically so it remains readable on a phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize readability and stacking order on mobile; avoid layouts that rely on large-screen interactions or force horizontal scrolling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standalone story formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: The MNR should be formatted in a way that it can function as a standalone story, instead of directing journalists to a separate folder to find assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the essential narrative and assets on the release page itself so journalists and readers don't need to hunt in separate folders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility compliance (overarching)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility compliance when using multimedia requires applying specific technical standards, such as captioning and alt text, to make content usable for all audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow accessibility standards to expand audience reach and reduce legal risk (e.g., ADA, Section 508); treat accessibility as required for multimedia assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video captioning (closed captions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deaf or hard-of-hearing users and mobile users watching video with the sound off need closed captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate, synchronized captions for all video assets; captions also aid indexing and mobile consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing a transcript of podcasts or audio clips allows users to read the content if they can't listen to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full transcripts for audio assets so non-listening users and assistive technologies can access the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alt text for images
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive alternative text allows screen readers to explain the visual content to blind or low-vision users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write meaningful alt text that conveys the purpose and key information of each image rather than decorative descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color contrast (WCAG contrast ratios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Text placed over images or colored backgrounds must meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines contrast ratios to remain readable for people with visual impairments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test foreground/background contrast and adjust colors or overlays to meet WCAG contrast requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO through text alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Search engines rely on captions, transcripts and alt text to index multimedia content; providing these text alternatives gives search crawlers more context, which can improve the release’s visibility in search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure captions, transcripts and alt text include relevant keywords and descriptive context to boost discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement actions (multimedia-specific metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track how many people played the video, clicked through the image gallery or downloaded the media kit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrument multimedia to capture specific engagement events (play, gallery click, download) rather than relying only on pageviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time on page
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess users' average time on page to determine whether the multimedia elements successfully hold the reader's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time-on-page alongside engagement events to judge whether assets are keeping users engaged; investigate if time drops off early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-through rates (CTRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor how many readers clicked the call to action button or followed links to your landing pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track CTA CTRs to measure conversion interest; align CTAs with the story so clicks are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset pickup (third-party reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which specific images or videos third-party outlets downloaded or embedded to see what was most valuable to journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor downloads/embeds and syndication to learn which assets resonate with journalists and publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use measurement to refine structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing these data points helps you refine your strategy for future releases. If users consistently drop off after the first paragraph, you might need to move your primary video higher up the page. If a certain type of infographic gets shared frequently, you know to prioritize that format in your next campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act on metrics: change asset placement, experiment with formats, and prioritize assets that drive engagement and pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place strongest visual immediately below headline / lead with the visual
rubrics_metrics.description: Structuring an MNR effectively requires placing the most compelling visual asset immediately below the headline or in the first paragraph to hook the audience instantly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put a striking image or dynamic video thumbnail near the top so journalists and readers are hooked within seconds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposeful multimedia (avoid irrelevant stock photos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only include multimedia that adds value and avoid stock photos that don't relate to the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assets that clarify, prove or humanize the story; remove filler visuals that dilute credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for scannability (short paragraphs, bullets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use short paragraphs and bullet points to break up the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format copy so readers can quickly scan for key facts; avoid dense blocks of text that repel mobile readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align the call to action (CTA) with content
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure your CTA is clear and relates to the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTAs should be obvious, relevant and placed where readers are primed to act; avoid mismatched or vague CTAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing: break up every 150–200 words with a visual
rubrics_metrics.description: Breaking up every 150-200 words of text with a visual element keeps the reader scrolling and helps the reader digest information in manageable chunks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent pacing rules to balance text and visuals, especially for mobile consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand-consistent multimedia (tone alignment)
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding how to incorporate images and videos into your content, remember to stay true to your brand's style. If your company tone is reserved, a flashy, animation-heavy release might feel disconnected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match multimedia style and intensity to brand voice; multimedia should enhance the message rather than distract from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use an MNR (use-case guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a multichannel news release when the announcement relies on visual evidence, emotional connection or complex data so audiences can fully understand it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include product launches (show product in action), corporate milestones (retrospective videos or timelines), brand storytelling (documentary-style video), and complex data announcements (infographics to simplify earnings or research).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine paid, owned and earned media to maximize impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective use of multichannel news releases makes an impact because they allow you to combine paid, owned and earned media to maximize your impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan distribution that leverages paid amplification, owned channels, and pitches to earn third-party pickup; use measurement to coordinate and optimize these channels.
